title: Five-field form (POSIX / Vixie baseline)

normative.title: POSIX.1-2017 crontab
normative.quote: The cron command shall ... minute, hour, day of the month, month, and day of the week

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: The one field-count every dialect accepts; the control vector for the family.

title: Six-field form: is the extra field seconds or year?

normative.title: Quartz CronExpression (1=SUN..7=SAT, '?' requirement, L/W/#)
normative.note: Quartz's six-field form is sec min hour dom month dow

normative.title: AWS EventBridge schedule expressions (6 fields, '?' required)
normative.note: EventBridge's six-field form is min hour dom month dow year

cases.label: seconds-leading
cases.note: Quartz, croner, cron-parser (6-field), robfig with WithSeconds(): the leading field is seconds.

cases.label: year-trailing
cases.note: AWS EventBridge, Spring: the trailing field is the year. Here the trailing token is '*', so the year is unrestricted and the expression means 10:15 daily.

cases.label: reject
cases.note: Strict five-field engines (POSIX crontab, cronsim default).

expect.note: The same six tokens denote 10:15:00 daily under one reading and 10:15 daily under another; both are silently accepted.

apscheduler3@tz2026a.error: ValueError: Wrong number of fields; got 6, expected 5

apscheduler3@tz2026c.error: ValueError: Wrong number of fields; got 6, expected 5

php-cron-expression@tz2026a.error: InvalidArgumentException: 6 is not a valid position

rationale: The six-field form is the worst kind of ambiguity: both readings parse, both produce plausible schedules, and the difference is only visible in the seconds field of the output. No document arbitrates between Quartz's and EventBridge's placement of the extra field.

title: Seconds granularity: every 15 seconds

normative.title: POSIX.1-2017 crontab
normative.note: POSIX cron has one-minute resolution and no seconds field

rationale: Sub-minute scheduling is the most common reason to leave the five-field form, and the point at which cron expressions stop being portable at all.

title: Six-field form with an unambiguous year token (2027)

normative.title: AWS EventBridge schedule expressions (6 fields, '?' required)

cases.label: year-trailing
cases.note: Reads 2027 as a year; the schedule is finite and has exactly one occurrence.

cases.label: seconds-leading
cases.note: Reads the leading '0' as seconds and then finds '2027' in the day-of-week field: out of range, so a parse error.

expect.note: This vector disambiguates the two six-field readings by construction: one accepts, the other must reject.

title: @reboot (an event, not a recurrence)

cases.label: reject
cases.note: A recurrence library has no startup event and should reject.

cases.label: empty
cases.note: Parse successfully and yield no occurrences.

cases.label: error-at-iteration
cases.note: Parse successfully, raise on first iteration.

expect.note: crontab(5) defines @reboot only in terms of the daemon's lifecycle, so a pure recurrence engine has no correct answer.
